nodes.title: Correctness of radix sort

nodes.summary: Let $b \ge 2$ and let every record carry a key that is a vector of $d$ digits in $\{0, \dots, b-1\}$. On an array of $n$ records, radix sort uses at most $d(7n + 3b)$ charged operations, where each counting-sort pass charges one unit for every counter initialization, key evaluation, counter read, counter write and output write.
nodes.title: Cost bound for radix sort

nodes.summary: Let $b \ge 2$ and let every record carry a key that is a vector of $d$ digits in $\{0, \dots, b-1\}$, most significant digit first, at positions $0, \dots, d-1$. Radix sort runs $d$ passes of stable counting sort on the array, the pass for position $i$ sorting by the digit of the key at position $i$, for $i = d-1, d-2, \dots, 0$, that is, from the least to the most significant digit.
